answer: Collateral is slashed jointly when correlated behavioural faults fire inside the same window. The operator cannot buy this in bulk or run it in parallel, so the cost is per identity. The ivory is the collateral at risk, the orchard the behavioural signature that groups identities, and the knoll the joint forfeiture that punishes the group: splitting into many orchard groups avoids the joint loss but scatters the ivory into smaller, individually useless stakes.
